fact_label: Territorial-tax facility for new foreign tax residents (first 4 years)
value_raw: Qualifying foreign nationals (must meet certain skill/expertise requirements) who become Indonesian tax residents are taxed only on Indonesian-sourced income (even if paid offshore) for their first 4 years as a tax resident; standard worldwide-income taxation applies after that window, or for anyone who doesn't qualify for the facility at all
notes: Landed 2026-07-18 (Kadek), filling the Income viability criterion's zero-fact gap. A genuinely undocumented-until-now structural fact for this project: unlike Panama/Costa Rica/Georgia-style territorial systems, Indonesia's territorial treatment is temporary (4 years) and conditional (skill-requirement-gated), not a standing feature — worth naming precisely rather than reading Indonesia as a territorial-tax country outright. Eligibility skill-requirement criteria themselves not independently pulled to a primary source this pass — PwC's own phrasing ("certain skill requirements") not further decomposed

value_raw: A foreign national becomes an Indonesian tax resident at 183 cumulative days present within any 12-month period, or on day 1 with documented intent to remain; presence under ~120 days generally means tax applies only to Indonesian-sourced income
notes: Cross-checked against PwC Tax Summaries (taxsummaries.pwc.com) the same session — anyone actually living in Bali full-time (the realistic shape of this project's own relocation scenario) crosses this threshold within their first year, making the territorial-facility row above and the worldwide-taxation row below directly load-bearing, not academic

fact_label: Worldwide-income taxation, progressive brackets (post-facility or non-qualifying resident)
value_raw: 0% to IDR 54M; 5% IDR 54-60M; 15% IDR 60-250M; 25% IDR 250-500M; 30% IDR 500M-5B; 35% above IDR 5B (annual)

fact_label: Restricted-nationality list — calling visa (multi-agency security-vetted pre-approval, excl. Israel — see its own dedicated row)
value_raw: AF, KP, LR, NG, SO
date: 2024-2025 (monitoring procedures finalized, per Middle East Monitor citing CNBC Indonesia)
notes: Extracted 2026-07-22 (Kadek), same harvest. Indonesia's 'calling visa' (visa lapor diri) is its most restrictive ordinary entry category, reserved for 6 nationalities: Afghanistan, Israel, Liberia, Nigeria, North Korea, Somalia. Israel deliberately split OUT of this list into its own dedicated fact row (ID:entry-restriction-israel-no-diplomatic-relations, below) because its own restriction rests on a materially different, more specific rationale (no diplomatic relations, not a generic high-risk-security screen) and carries its own document_conditional_note disclosure the other 5 don't share -- same split-out precedent Morocco's Ukraine/Venezuela rows already established in this project when treatment genuinely differs within one nominal list. Entry for all 6 nationalities permitted only via Soekarno-Hatta (Jakarta) or I Gusti Ngurah Rai (Bali) airports; reviewed by a multi-agency coordination team (immigration, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, intelligence/BAIS, police, military); prior Directorate General of Immigration (Jakarta) approval required before a visa application can be filed; processing weeks to months. Cross-corroborated: embassyinformation.com, visa-indonesia.com's dedicated calling-visa guide, Middle East Monitor (citing CNBC Indonesia immigration-intelligence data). No day-count figure found common to all 5 remaining nationalities -- entry_max_days left unmapped/null rather than guessed. imigrasi.go.id/evisa.imigrasi.go.id both HTTP 403 this session.

fact_label: Entry restriction — Israel (no diplomatic relations, calling visa)

notes: PRIORITY row, Cap's own direct catch (2026-07-21 late night, tracking log 2026-07-21-Cap-indonesiaisrael): 'did we not have data on indonesia being awkward for israelis?' -- real gap, zero prior vault capture (ID.jsonl 0 hits, Indonesia/*.md 0 hits before this pass). A named scope seam, not a research failure: Kadek's 2026-07-11 first pass never covered nationality rules at all; [specialist] 2026-07-16 Israeli-passport pass was deliberately scoped to the 10 then-active candidates, Indonesia outside that set (her own honest flag at the time). Indonesia has no diplomatic relations with Israel. Israeli passport holders sit on the same 'calling visa' list as Afghanistan/Liberia/Nigeria/North Korea/Somalia (ID:restricted-nationality-list-calling-visa-tier), split into this own dedicated row because the practical reality goes further than the shared list entry and rests on a distinct rationale (diplomatic non-relations, not a generic security screen): Indonesia's own immigration-intelligence data (via CNBC Indonesia, reported by Middle East Monitor 2026-01-08) shows only 51 calling visas issued to Israeli nationals in the ~11 months through 2025-11-30 -- Israel ranked 4th among calling-visa recipient nationalities, behind Nigeria, Somalia, Afghanistan. Stated approved purposes: business discussions, purchases, exhibitions, meetings, tourism, private visits by elderly travelers. Checked directly and found NONE: no religious-tourism or pilgrimage carve-out for Israeli nationals specifically -- a real checked-and-absent result, not silence. Tier call, named as a open item: rendered visa-required rather than suspended -- entry is not a formal legal suspension (unlike the US's Proclamation 10998 partial suspension of Venezuelan entry, this project's other suspended-tier precedent; a visa can genuinely be obtained, people do get through), so suspended would overstate the legal mechanism; but bare visa-required alone would understate the real barrier that token implies elsewhere in this table (51 approvals over ~11 months against ~9.7M Israelis is a near-total practical bar for ordinary tourism). Resolved via document_conditional_note carrying the severity -- this extends that field's usage beyond its two ratified senses ([on file] 8Z.2, both built for disclosing a RELIEF/facility, not a restriction) -- a genuine judgment call, not a quiet reinterpretation, flagged for [specialist]/[specialist] review. Cross-corroborated: embassyinformation.com, middleeastmonitor.com (2026-01-08, citing CNBC Indonesia), visa-indonesia.com's calling-visa guide, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_policy_of_Indonesia. imigrasi.go.id/evisa.imigrasi.go.id both HTTP 403 this session -- aggregator-recheck tier, not primary-institutional.
document_conditional_note: Indonesia has no diplomatic relations with Israel. Entry requires prior approval from the Directorate General of Immigration in Jakarta plus a multi-agency 'calling visa' review (immigration, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, intelligence/BAIS, police, military); permitted only via Soekarno-Hatta (Jakarta) or I Gusti Ngurah Rai (Bali) airports. Practically severe, not merely bureaucratic: only 51 calling visas were issued to Israeli nationals in the ~11 months through 2025-11-30 (immigration-intelligence data via CNBC Indonesia/Middle East Monitor) -- a near-total practical bar for ordinary tourism, though not a formal legal suspension. No religious-tourism or pilgrimage carve-out found.
